043/**
044 * Parent class for all Juneau parsers.
045 *
046 * <h2 class='topic'>Valid data conversions</h2>
047 * <p>
048 * Parsers can parse any parsable POJO types, as specified in the <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/PojoCategories">POJO Categories</a>.
049 *
050 * <p>
051 * Some examples of conversions are shown below...
052 * </p>
053 * <table class='styled'>
054 *    <caption>Supported input data types</caption>
055 *    <tr>
056 *       <th>Data type</th>
057 *       <th>Class type</th>
058 *       <th>JSON example</th>
059 *       <th>XML example</th>
060 *       <th>Class examples</th>
061 *    </tr>
062 *    <tr>
063 *       <td>object</td>
064 *       <td>Maps, Java beans</td>
065 *       <td class='code'>{name:<js>'John Smith'</js>,age:21}</td>
066 *       <td class='code'><xt>&lt;object&gt;
067 *    &lt;name</xt> <xa>type</xa>=<xs>'string'</xs><xt>&gt;</xt>John Smith<xt>&lt;/name&gt;
068 *    &lt;age</xt> <xa>type</xa>=<xs>'number'</xs><xt>&gt;</xt>21<xt>&lt;/age&gt;
069 * &lt;/object&gt;</xt></td>
070 *       <td class='code'>HashMap, TreeMap&lt;String,Integer&gt;</td>
071 *    </tr>
072 *    <tr>
073 *       <td>array</td>
074 *       <td>Collections, Java arrays</td>
075 *       <td class='code'>[1,2,3]</td>
076 *       <td class='code'><xt>&lt;array&gt;
077 *    &lt;number&gt;</xt>1<xt>&lt;/number&gt;
078 *    &lt;number&gt;</xt>2<xt>&lt;/number&gt;
079 *    &lt;number&gt;</xt>3<xt>&lt;/number&gt;
080 * &lt;/array&gt;</xt></td>
081 *       <td class='code'>List&lt;Integer&gt;, <jk>int</jk>[], Float[], Set&lt;Person&gt;</td>
082 *    </tr>
083 *    <tr>
084 *       <td>number</td>
085 *       <td>Numbers</td>
086 *       <td class='code'>123</td>
087 *       <td class='code'><xt>&lt;number&gt;</xt>123<xt>&lt;/number&gt;</xt></td>
088 *       <td class='code'>Integer, Long, Float, <jk>int</jk></td>
089 *    </tr>
090 *    <tr>
091 *       <td>boolean</td>
092 *       <td>Booleans</td>
093 *       <td class='code'><jk>true</jk></td>
094 *       <td class='code'><xt>&lt;boolean&gt;</xt>true<xt>&lt;/boolean&gt;</xt></td>
095 *       <td class='code'>Boolean</td>
096 *    </tr>
097 *    <tr>
098 *       <td>string</td>
099 *       <td>CharSequences</td>
100 *       <td class='code'><js>'foobar'</js></td>
101 *       <td class='code'><xt>&lt;string&gt;</xt>foobar<xt>&lt;/string&gt;</xt></td>
102 *       <td class='code'>String, StringBuilder</td>
103 *    </tr>
104 * </table>
105 *
106 * <p>
107 * In addition, any class types with {@link ObjectSwap ObjectSwaps} associated with them on the registered
108 * bean context can also be passed in.
109 *
110 * <p>
111 * For example, if a {@link CalendarFormat}-driven swap is used to generalize {@code Calendar} objects to {@code String}
112 * objects.
113 * When registered with this parser, you can construct {@code Calendar} objects from {@code Strings} using the
114 * following syntax...
115 * <p class='bjava'>
116 *    Calendar <jv>calendar</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"'Sun Mar 03 04:05:06 EST 2001'"</js>, GregorianCalendar.<jk>class</jk>);
117 * </p>
118 *
119 * <p>
120 * If <code>Object.<jk>class</jk></code> is specified as the target type, then the parser automatically determines the
121 * data types and generates the following object types...
122 * <table class='styled'>
123 *    <caption>JSON types and the object types they produce</caption>
124 *    <tr><th>JSON type</th><th>Class type</th></tr>
125 *    <tr><td>object</td><td>{@link JsonMap}</td></tr>
126 *    <tr><td>array</td><td>{@link JsonList}</td></tr>
127 *    <tr><td>number</td><td>{@link Number}<br>(depending on length and format, could be {@link Integer},
128 *       {@link Double}, {@link Float}, etc...)</td></tr>
129 *    <tr><td>boolean</td><td>{@link Boolean}</td></tr>
130 *    <tr><td>string</td><td>{@link String}</td></tr>
131 * </table>
132 *
133 * <h2 class='section'>Notes:</h2><ul>
134 *    <li class='note'>This class is thread safe and reusable.
135 * </ul>
136 *
137 * <h2 class='section'>See Also:</h2><ul>
138 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/SerializersAndParsers">Serializers and Parsers</a>
139
140 * </ul>
141 */
142@SuppressWarnings({
143   "java:S1192", // Duplicated literals (argument/property names) read more clearly inline than as constants
144   "rawtypes" // createParserBuilder() returns the raw Builder because the builder subtype is only known reflectively.
145})
146public class Parser extends MarshallingContextable {
147
148   /**
149    * Builder class.
150    */
151   @SuppressWarnings({
152      "java:S119" // 'SELF' (CRTP self-type) is intentional and clearer than a single-letter name.
153   })
154   public abstract static class Builder<SELF extends Builder<SELF>> extends MarshallingContextable.Builder<SELF> {
155
156      private boolean autoCloseStreams;
157      private boolean trimStrings;
158      private boolean unbuffered;
159      private Class<? extends ParserListener> listener;
160      private int debugOutputLines;
161      private String consumes;
162      private Nulls nulls;
163
164      /**
165       * Constructor, default settings.
166       */
167      protected Builder() {
168         autoCloseStreams = env("Parser.autoCloseStreams", false);
169         trimStrings = env("Parser.trimStrings", false);
170         unbuffered = env("Parser.unbuffered", false);
171         debugOutputLines = env("Parser.debugOutputLines", 5);
172         listener = null;
173         consumes = null;
174         nulls = Nulls.NOT_SET;
175      }
176
177      /**
178       * Copy constructor.
179       *
180       * @param copyFrom The builder to copy from.
181       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
182       */
183      protected Builder(Builder<?> copyFrom) {
184         super(copyFrom);
185         autoCloseStreams = copyFrom.autoCloseStreams;
186         trimStrings = copyFrom.trimStrings;
187         unbuffered = copyFrom.unbuffered;
188         debugOutputLines = copyFrom.debugOutputLines;
189         listener = copyFrom.listener;
190         consumes = copyFrom.consumes;
191         nulls = copyFrom.nulls;
192      }
193
194      /**
195       * Copy constructor.
196       *
197       * @param copyFrom The bean to copy from.
198       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
199       */
200      protected Builder(Parser copyFrom) {
201         super(copyFrom);
202         autoCloseStreams = copyFrom.autoCloseStreams;
203         trimStrings = copyFrom.trimStrings;
204         unbuffered = copyFrom.unbuffered;
205         debugOutputLines = copyFrom.debugOutputLines;
206         listener = copyFrom.listener;
207         consumes = copyFrom.consumes;
208         nulls = copyFrom.nulls;
209      }
210
211      /**
212       * Auto-close streams.
213       *
214       * <p>
215       * When enabled, <l>InputStreams</l> and <l>Readers</l> passed into parsers will be closed
216       * after parsing is complete.
217       *
218       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
219       * <p class='bjava'>
220       *    <jc>// Create a parser using strict mode.</jc>
221       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
222       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
223       *       .autoCloseStreams()
224       *       .build();
225       *
226       *    Reader <jv>myReader</jv> = <jk>new</jk> FileReader(<js>"/tmp/myfile.json"</js>);
227       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>myReader</jv>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
228       *
229       *    <jsm>assertTrue</jsm>(<jv>myReader</jv>.isClosed());
230       * </p>
231       *
232       * @return This object.
233       */
234      public SELF autoCloseStreams() {
235         return autoCloseStreams(true);
236      }
237
238      /**
239       * Same as {@link #autoCloseStreams()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
240       *
241       * @param value The value for this setting.
242       * @return This object.
243       */
244      public SELF autoCloseStreams(boolean value) {
245         autoCloseStreams = value;
246         return self();
247      }
248
249      @Override /* Overridden from Context.Builder<?> */
250      public Parser build() {
251         return build(Parser.class);
252      }
253
254      /**
255       * Specifies the media type that this parser consumes.
256       *
257       * <p>
258       * <b>Token streams:</b> this setting is not honored by {@link TokenReadable#readTokens(Object) readTokens}
259       * &mdash; media-type metadata is informational, not behavioral.
260       *
261       * @param value The value for this setting.
262       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty string, no media types will be specified).
263       * @return This object.
264       */
265      public SELF consumes(String value) {
266         consumes = value;
267         return self();
268      }
269
270      @Override /* Overridden from Context.Builder<?> */
271      public abstract SELF copy();
272
273      /**
274       * Debug output lines.
275       *
276       * <p>
277       * When parse errors occur, this specifies the number of lines of input before and after the
278       * error location to be printed as part of the exception message.
279       *
280       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
281       * <p class='bjava'>
282       *    <jc>// Create a parser whose exceptions print out 100 lines before and after the parse error location.</jc>
283       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
284       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
285       *       .debug()  <jc>// Enable debug mode to capture Reader contents as strings.</jc>
286       *       .debugOuputLines(100)
287       *       .build();
288       *
289       *    Reader <jv>myReader</jv> = <jk>new</jk> FileReader(<js>"/tmp/mybadfile.json"</js>);
290       *    <jk>try</jk> {
291       *       <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>myReader</jv>, Object.<jk>class</jk>);
292       *    } <jk>catch</jk> (ParseException <jv>e</jv>) {
293       *       System.<jsf>err</jsf>.println(<jv>e</jv>.getMessage());  <jc>// Will display 200 lines of the output.</jc>
294       *    }
295       * </p>
296       *
297       * <p>
298       * <b>Token streams:</b> this setting is not honored by {@link TokenReadable#readTokens(Object) readTokens}
299       * &mdash; it controls error-message formatting on the POJO databind path; the cursor uses its own
300       * exception text.
301       *
302       * @param value
303       *    The new value for this property.
304       *    <br>The default value is <c>5</c>.
305       * @return This object.
306       */
307      public SELF debugOutputLines(int value) {
308         debugOutputLines = value;
309         return self();
310      }
311
312      /**
313       * Returns the current value for the 'consumes' property.
314       *
315       * @return The current value for the 'consumes' property, or <jk>null</jk> if not specified.
316       */
317      public String getConsumes() { return consumes; }
318
319      @Override /* Overridden from Context.Builder<?> */
320      public HashKey hashKey() {
321         // @formatter:off
322         return HashKey.of(
323            super.hashKey(),
324            autoCloseStreams,
325            trimStrings,
326            unbuffered,
327            debugOutputLines,
328            listener,
329            consumes,
330            nulls
331         );
332         // @formatter:on
333      }
334
335      /**
336       * Parser listener.
337       *
338       * <p>
339       * Class used to listen for errors and warnings that occur during parsing.
340       *
341       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
342       * <p class='bjava'>
343       *    <jc>// Define our parser listener.</jc>
344       *    <jc>// Simply captures all unknown bean property events.</jc>
345       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyParserListener <jk>extends</jk> ParserListener {
346       *
347       *       <jc>// A simple property to store our events.</jc>
348       *       <jk>public</jk> List&lt;String&gt; <jf>events</jf> = <jk>new</jk> LinkedList&lt;&gt;();
349       *
350       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
351       *       <jk>public</jk> &lt;T&gt; <jk>void</jk> onUnknownBeanProperty(ParserSession <jv>session</jv>, String <jv>propertyName</jv>, Class&lt;T&gt; <jv>beanClass</jv>, T <jv>bean</jv>) {
352       *          Position <jv>position</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.getPosition();
353       *          <jf>events</jf>.add(<jv>propertyName</jv> + <js>","</js> + <jv>position</jv>.getLine() + <js>","</js> + <jv>position</jv>.getColumn());
354       *       }
355       *    }
356       *
357       *    <jc>// Create a parser using our listener.</jc>
358       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
359       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
360       *       .listener(MyParserListener.<jk>class</jk>)
361       *       .build();
362       *
363       *    <jc>// Create a session object.</jc>
364       *    <jc>// Needed because listeners are created per-session.</jc>
365       *    <jk>try</jk> (ReaderParserSession <jv>session</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.createSession()) {
366       *
367       *       <jc>// Parse some JSON object.</jc>
368       *       MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.read(<js>"{...}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
369       *
370       *       <jc>// Get the listener.</jc>
371       *       MyParserListener <jv>listener</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.getListener(MyParserListener.<jk>class</jk>);
372       *
373       *       <jc>// Dump the results to the console.</jc>
374       *       Json5.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>.println(<jv>listener</jv>.<jf>events</jf>);
375       *    }
376       * </p>
377       *
378       * <p>
379       * <b>Token streams:</b> this setting is not honored by {@link TokenReadable#readTokens(Object) readTokens}
380       * &mdash; listeners are POJO-level observers with no token-layer analog.
381       *
382       * @param value The new value for this property.
383       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (no listener will be used, listener methods will not be called).
384       * @return This object.
385       */
386      public SELF listener(Class<? extends ParserListener> value) {
387         listener = value;
388         return self();
389      }
390
391      /**
392       * Sets the default per-property null-coercion policy applied during parsing.
393       *
394       * <p>
395       * Juneau's analog of Jackson's
396       * <c>ObjectMapper.setDefaultSetterInfo(JsonSetter.Value.forValueNulls(...))</c>.
397       * Applied as the fallback when no per-property
398       * {@link MarshalledProp#nulls() @MarshalledProp(nulls=…)} is configured.
399       *
400       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
401       * <p class='bjava'>
402       *    <jc>// Substitute the empty value for any property whose wire value is null.</jc>
403       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
404       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
405       *       .nulls(Nulls.<jsf>EMPTY</jsf>)
406       *       .build();
407       * </p>
408       *
409       * @param value The new value for this property.
410       *    <br>{@code null} or {@link Nulls#NOT_SET} disables the default (each property falls back to
411       *    {@link Nulls#LEAVE}).
412       * @return This object.
413       * @since 10.0.0
414       */
415      public SELF nulls(Nulls value) {
416         nulls = value == null ? Nulls.NOT_SET : value;
417         return self();
418      }
419
420      /**
421       * Returns the current context-level {@link Nulls} default configured on this builder.
422       *
423       * @return The current value (never <jk>null</jk>; {@link Nulls#NOT_SET} when unconfigured).
424       * @since 10.0.0
425       */
426      public Nulls getNulls() { return nulls == null ? Nulls.NOT_SET : nulls; }
427
428      /**
429       * Trim parsed strings.
430       *
431       * <p>
432       * When enabled, string values will be trimmed of whitespace using {@link String#trim()} before being added to
433       * the POJO.
434       *
435       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
436       * <p class='bjava'>
437       *    <jc>// Create a parser with trim-strings enabled.</jc>
438       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
439       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
440       *       .trimStrings()
441       *       .build();
442       *
443       *    <jc>// Use it.</jc>
444       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <js>"{' foo ':' bar '}"</js>;
445       *    Map&lt;String,String&gt; <jv>myMap</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, HashMap.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>);
446       *
447       *    <jc>// Make sure strings are parsed.</jc>
448       *    <jsm>assertEquals</jsm>(<js>"bar"</js>, <jv>myMap</jv>.get(<js>"foo"</js>));
449       * </p>
450       *
451       * @return This object.
452       */
453      public SELF trimStrings() {
454         return trimStrings(true);
455      }
456
457      /**
458       * Same as {@link #trimStrings()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
459       *
460       * @param value The value for this setting.
461       * @return This object.
462       */
463      public SELF trimStrings(boolean value) {
464         trimStrings = value;
465         return self();
466      }
467
468      /**
469       * Unbuffered.
470       *
471       * <p>
472       * When enabled, don't use internal buffering during parsing.
473       *
474       * <p>
475       * This is useful in cases when you want to parse the same input stream or reader multiple times
476       * because it may contain multiple independent POJOs to parse.
477       * <br>Buffering would cause the parser to read past the current POJO in the stream.
478       *
479       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
480       * <p class='bjava'>
481       *    <jc>// Create a parser using strict mode.</jc>
482       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser.
483       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
484       *       .unbuffered(<jk>true</jk>)
485       *       .build();
486       *
487       *    <jc>// If you're calling parse on the same input multiple times, use a session instead of the parser directly.</jc>
488       *    <jc>// It's more efficient because we don't need to recalc the session settings again. </jc>
489       *    ReaderParserSession <jv>session</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.createSession();
490       *
491       *    <jc>// Read input with multiple POJOs</jc>
492       *    Reader <jv>json</jv> = <jk>new</jk> StringReader(<js>"{foo:'bar'}{foo:'baz'}"</js>);
493       *    MyBean <jv>myBean1</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
494       *    MyBean <jv>myBean2</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
495       * </p>
496       *
497       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
498       *    <li class='note'>
499       *       This only allows for multi-input streams for the following parsers:
500       *       <ul>
501       *          <li class='jc'>{@link JsonParser}
502       *          <li class='jc'>{@link UonParser}
503       *       </ul>
504       *       It has no effect on the following parsers:
505       *       <ul>
506       *          <li class='jc'>{@link MsgPackParser} - It already doesn't use buffering.
507       *          <li class='jc'>{@link XmlParser}, {@link HtmlParser} - These use StAX which doesn't allow for more than one root element anyway.
508       *          <li>RDF parsers - These read everything into an internal model before any parsing begins.
509       *       </ul>
510       * </ul>
511       *
512       * @return This object.
513       */
514      public SELF unbuffered() {
515         return unbuffered(true);
516      }
517
518      /**
519       * Same as {@link #unbuffered()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
520       *
521       * @param value The value for this setting.
522       * @return This object.
523       */
524      public SELF unbuffered(boolean value) {
525         unbuffered = value;
526         return self();
527      }
528
529
530   }

565   /**
566    * Creates a new builder for this object.
567    *
568    * @return A new builder.
569    */

571      "java:S1452" // Self-typed builder: Builder<?> is the only non-raw, leaf-free return; chaining + build() unaffected.

577   /**
578    * Instantiates a builder of the specified parser class.
579    *
580    * <p>
581    * Looks for a public static method called <c>create</c> that returns an object that can be passed into a public
582    * or protected constructor of the class.
583    *
584    * @param c The builder to create.
585    *    <br>Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
586    * @return A new builder.
587    */
588   public static Builder createParserBuilder(Class<? extends Parser> c) {
589      return (Builder)Context.createBuilder(c);
590   }

592   protected final boolean autoCloseStreams;
593   protected final boolean trimStrings;
594   protected final boolean unbuffered;
595   protected final int debugOutputLines;
596   protected final Class<? extends ParserListener> listener;
597   protected final String consumes;
598   protected final Nulls nulls;
599   private final List<MediaType> consumesArray;
600
601   /**
602    * Constructor.

757   /**
758    * Parses input into the specified object type.
759    *
760    * <p>
761    * The type can be a simple type (e.g. beans, strings, numbers) or parameterized type (collections/maps).
762    *
763    * <h4 class='section'>Examples:</h4>
764    * <p class='bjava'>
765    *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>;
766    *
767    *    <jc>// Parse into a linked-list of strings.</jc>
768    *    List <jv>list1</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, LinkedList.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>);
769    *
770    *    <jc>// Parse into a linked-list of beans.</jc>
771    *    List <jv>list2</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, LinkedList.<jk>class</jk>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
772    *
773    *    <jc>// Parse into a linked-list of linked-lists of strings.</jc>
774    *    List <jv>list3</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, LinkedList.<jk>class</jk>, LinkedList.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>);
775    *
776    *    <jc>// Parse into a map of string keys/values.</jc>
777    *    Map <jv>map1</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, TreeMap.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>);
778    *
779    *    <jc>// Parse into a map containing string keys and values of lists containing beans.</jc>
780    *    Map <jv>map2</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, TreeMap.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>, List.<jk>class</jk>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
781    * </p>
782    *
783    * <p>
784    * <c>Collection</c> classes are assumed to be followed by zero or one objects indicating the element type.
785    *
786    * <p>
787    * <c>Map</c> classes are assumed to be followed by zero or two meta objects indicating the key and value types.
788    *
789    * <p>
790    * The array can be arbitrarily long to indicate arbitrarily complex data structures.
791    *
792    * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
793    *    <li class='note'>
794    *       Use the {@link #read(Object, Class)} method instead if you don't need a parameterized map/collection.
795    * </ul>
796    *
797    * @param <T> The class type of the object to create.
798    * @param input
799    *    The input.
800    *    <br>Character-based parsers can handle the following input class types:
801    *    <ul>
802    *       <li><jk>null</jk>
803    *       <li>{@link Reader}
804    *       <li>{@link CharSequence}
805    *       <li>{@link InputStream} containing UTF-8 encoded text (or charset defined by
806    *          {@link ReaderParser.Builder#streamCharset(Charset)} property value).
807    *       <li><code><jk>byte</jk>[]</code> containing UTF-8 encoded text (or charset defined by
808    *          {@link ReaderParser.Builder#streamCharset(Charset)} property value).
809    *    </ul>
810    *    <br>Stream-based parsers can handle the following input class types:
811    *    <ul>
812    *       <li><jk>null</jk>
813    *       <li>{@link InputStream}
814    *       <li><code><jk>byte</jk>[]</code>
815    *       <li>{@link CharSequence} containing encoded bytes according to the {@link InputStreamParser.Builder#binaryFormat(BinaryFormat)} setting.
816    *    </ul>
817    * @param type
818    *    The object type to create.
819    *    <br>Can be any of the following: {@link ClassMeta}, {@link Class}, {@link ParameterizedType}, {@link GenericArrayType}
820    * @param args
821    *    The type arguments of the class if it's a collection or map.
822    *    <br>Can be any of the following: {@link ClassMeta}, {@link Class}, {@link ParameterizedType}, {@link GenericArrayType}
823    *    <br>Ignored if the main type is not a map or collection.
824    * @return The parsed object.
825    * @throws ParseException Malformed input encountered.
826    * @throws IOException Thrown by underlying stream.
827    * @see MarshallingSession#getClassMeta(Type,Type...) for argument syntax for maps and collections.
828    */
829   public final <T> T read(Object input, Type type, Type...args) throws ParseException, IOException {
830      return getSession().read(input, type, args);
831   }
